question: Which type of hypersensitivity reaction is serum sickness?
explanation: Serum sickness is caused by immune complexes building up in the body, which makes it a type III hypersensitivity reaction. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why does it take several days or weeks for serum sickness symptoms to show up after exposure?

options.A: White blood cells are temporarily paralyzed by the animal serum
options.B: The body needs time to build antibodies against foreign proteins
options.C: The liver slowly digests the serum proteins before they become active
options.D: Foreign proteins hide inside red blood cells for a long period

explanation: Symptoms take time to appear because the immune system needs a few days to generate antibodies against the foreign proteins. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h1)

question: What gets trapped in body tissues during a serum sickness reaction?
explanation: The condition happens when clusters of antigens and antibodies join together and get trapped in small blood vessels and tissues. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h2)

question: What happens after immune complexes get trapped in small blood vessels?

options.A: The complement cascade triggers local inflammation and tissue injury
options.B: Blood flow instantly stops and causes permanent tissue necrosis
options.C: Foreign proteins dissolve harmlessly into the surrounding muscle tissue
options.D: Platelets aggregate to repair the vessel wall without any inflammation

explanation: When immune complexes get stuck, they trigger the body's complement system, leading to local inflammation and injury to the tissue. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h2)

question: Which common treatment is a well-known trigger for serum sickness in clinical practice?
explanation: Antivenoms made from animal blood contain foreign proteins that can trigger serum sickness in snakebite patients. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h3)

question: How do non-protein drugs like penicillin sometimes cause a reaction similar to serum sickness?

options.A: They act as haptens and bind to host proteins to form new antigens
options.B: They alter the pH of the blood to damage kidney glomeruli directly
options.C: They directly destroy circulating white blood cells within minutes
options.D: They block the normal production of antibodies in the bone marrow

explanation: Small drug molecules attach to the body's own proteins, tricking the immune system into treating them like foreign invaders. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h3)

question: Which symptom is almost always present in patients with serum sickness?
explanation: Pain affecting multiple large joints is one of the most common and noticeable signs of serum sickness. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h4)

question: What does the skin rash in serum sickness typically look like?
explanation: The rash usually appears as itchy hives or flat, red spots spreading across the skin. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h4)

question: Why is a urine test (urinalysis) important when checking for serum sickness?

options.A: It tracks the daily metabolism of therapeutic horse serum
options.B: It confirms the presence of antibodies in the urinary bladder
options.C: It measures the exact concentration of circulating foreign antigens
options.D: It detects early signs of renal involvement like proteinuria

explanation: Because immune complexes can affect the kidneys, checking the urine helps spot early kidney stress, such as protein in the urine. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h5)

question: Which blood test is used to check for general inflammation in the body?
explanation: Tests like C-reactive protein help doctors measure the level of inflammation happening inside the body. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h5)

question: What is the very first step in managing a patient with suspected serum sickness?

options.B: Discontinue the triggering drug or antiserum
options.C: Apply cold ice packs to affected joints
options.D: Administer a high dose of oral antibiotics

explanation: Stopping the medication or antivenom causing the reaction is the most important step to help the patient recover. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h6)

question: When are systemic corticosteroids usually prescribed for serum sickness?

options.A: As a prophylactic measure before any antivenom injection
options.B: To replace antihistamines in patients with chronic kidney disease
options.C: For severe cases with systemic symptoms and organ involvement
options.D: Only when skin rashes fail to respond to cold water baths

explanation: Doctors use corticosteroids in more severe cases to quickly calm down widespread inflammation and protect organs. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h6)

question: Which nursing action helps relieve joint discomfort in a patient with serum sickness?

options.A: Applying warm or cool compresses to affected joints
options.B: Encouraging high-impact aerobic exercises twice daily
options.C: Placing tight elastic bandages around all sore limbs
options.D: Restricting all fluid intake to reduce joint swelling

explanation: Warm or cool compresses provide safe, non-drug relief for painful, swollen joints. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h7)

question: What is a crucial piece of advice a nurse must give a recovering serum sickness patient before discharge?

options.A: Restrict dietary protein intake to prevent new immune complexes
options.B: Perform daily urine cultures at home using sterile kits
options.C: Take prophylactic antibiotics daily for the rest of their life
options.D: Avoid the triggering drug and inform providers of the allergy

explanation: Teaching the patient to stay away from the triggering medication prevents future, potentially worse allergic reactions. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h7)

question: What is the usual outlook (prognosis) for someone diagnosed with serum sickness?

options.A: Guarded, requiring lifelong kidney replacement therapy
options.B: Poor, with a high rate of permanent joint paralysis
options.C: Unpredictable, often progressing to chronic anaphylaxis
options.D: Excellent, because the condition is usually self-limiting

explanation: Most patients get better completely within a few weeks once the offending substance is stopped. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h8)

question: Which rare kidney problem can happen if immune complexes build up in the kidneys?
explanation: When immune complexes get trapped in the tiny filtering units of the kidneys, it can cause inflammation known as glomerulonephritis. [learn more](GST114_U4_T10#GST114_U4_T10_h8)
